Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- The FOMC’s statement is constructive but cautious. SLOOS points to mixed credit supply: domestic banks expect to ease standards for C&I loans and see improving C&I asset quality, which supports the Committee’s outlook for continued labor-market strength and could help alleviate “soft” business fixed investment.
- Offsetting this, banks expect to tighten standards for CRE (including construction/land development) and for auto loans, and they expect asset quality to deteriorate in credit cards and autos—consistent with some consumer-credit headwinds.
- Housing finance looks steady-to-easier for prime segments (easing for GSE-eligible and nonconforming jumbo RRE), with little change expected for GSE-eligible/HELOCs, which modestly supports consumption and residential activity.
- Foreign banks report weaker business loan demand and expect broader tightening (C&I, small firms, CRE), adding a note of caution.

Netting these cross-currents, SLOOS slightly tempers the initially mildly positive tone: easing in core business credit and some mortgages is a plus, but tightening and asset-quality concerns in CRE/consumer, along with foreign-bank caution, argue for a more guarded near-term outlook. Monetary policy remaining accommodative is consistent with this mix.
